name: Elasto-Dicht Hermannsdorfer GmbH
summary: Elasto-Dicht Hermannsdorfer is a family-owned seal maker founded in 1987, with 45 staff and about EUR 22.9 M turnover. It is financially solid (equity 38.9 %, credit index stable at 167), and the owner is personally involved, even offering an open-book calculation. We are a tiny account for them (0.2 % of their turnover), and they have said they are reviewing small accounts to focus on volume customers. Our kit-bundling plan (about 25,000 kits a year) is the lever that can turn us into a customer worth keeping.

situation.decision_maker: Owner decides price; sales director shapes account strategy; new inside-sales colleague handles day-to-day contact only

negotiation_pattern: Moderate annual renewal asks, settling well below them. Mean ask 2.8 %, mean settled 0.83 %. It accepted 0 % in the 2023 and 2024 rounds (asks 1.1-2.7 %). In Nov/Dec 2025 it asked 5.4 % and 4.0 % and got 2.4 % and 2.6 %. The 2025 requests were dated 24 Nov and 1 Dec, after the 90-day notice point in clause 3.1. It does not dig in on price. It responds to fact-based discussion and offered to show its hourly rates and material costs.
wants: Volume and relevance as a customer (they are culling small accounts)
Fair, respectful treatment and payment on time (we pay late 84 % of the time)
Long-term, steady business with predictable call-offs
Price settled on its transparent cost basis rather than by pressure
protects: unit_price for small, scattered volumes (won't subsidise a minor account)
Its open-book calculation as the reference point: expect it to defend hourly rates and material once shown
lead_time_days already at 7 days; little room left

trades.give: volume_per_year up: award the full kit (lip seal 50 % to 100 %, aramid gasket 0 % to 100 %, O-ring set stays 100 %)
trades.get: unit_price freeze for 2027 on 340020/340040 plus a kit price, with gasket at or below the 2025 quote of EUR 1.97
trades.why: Turns us from a small account under review into a volume customer, which is exactly what they said they focus on.

trades.give: contract_months up: extend the framework beyond 2027-06-30 (e.g. +24 months) with a kit forecast
trades.get: Prices fixed for the extended term, no index_clause
trades.why: Family firm values long-term commitment; the current contract only rolls by 12 months.

trades.give: payment_days kept at 30 but a firm commitment to pay on time
trades.why: Costs us nothing; it fixes a fairness irritant, since we pay late 84 % of the time (2.8 days on average).

trades.give: Accept the owner's offer of an open-book review of the calculation
trades.get: Kit pricing built bottom-up, sharing the efficiency of fewer, larger kit deliveries
trades.why: The owner offered this himself; accepting it shows respect and anchors price on facts.

trades.get: ppm_commitment ≤ 250 and OTD 95 % per the quality agreement; keep chargeback at EUR 150 per complaint
trades.why: The trend is improving (ppm 371 to 291, OTD 91.8 %) but OTD is still below the 95 % target.

arguments.point: The kit project makes us a meaningfully larger customer: 25,000 kits a year means 50,000 O-ring sets, 25,000 gaskets and 50,000 lip seals from one source.
Prices are fixed per calendar year. Changes need written notice at least 90 days before year end, which is about 2 Oct 2026. A later increase request has no contractual basis for 2027.
Recognise the improving scorecard (score 94.5, class A, ppm down to 291) and frame the kit award as a reward for that progress.
Take up the owner's open-book offer to settle the kit price fairly and transparently.
The 2025 increases (2.4 % and 2.6 %) were already granted for 2026, so a further rise is hard to justify.

avoid: Hard pressure or ultimatums; an owner-led firm digs in, and with 0.2 % share they can simply drop us
Threatening to resource the O-ring set: there is no alternative source and drinking-water approval is required
Overstating our size; they know we are small
Ignoring our late-payment record or asking for longer payment terms
Negotiating only through the new inside-sales contact; involve the owner for price
tone: Respectful, personal and partnership-oriented. Address the owner, acknowledge progress, and present the kit as a long-term commitment, not a squeeze.
red_flags: Small-account review: risk they deprioritise us or price us out if no volume comes
Single source for part:340020 (drinking-water EPDM O-ring set) with no alternative, so supply risk if they walk away
OTD 91.8 % is still below the 95 % target; 13 complaints in the last 12 months (EUR 1,500 recharged)
Possible increase notice arriving right at the 90-day deadline (~2 Oct 2026)

evidence.claim: Family-owned, 45 staff, EUR 22.9 M turnover, equity 38.9 %, credit index 167 unchanged over 12 months
We are 0.2 % of its turnover (spend about EUR 46 k a year)
Sales director said they are reviewing small accounts and focusing on volume customers
Owner offered to walk us through hourly rates and material calculation
Kit plan: about 25,000 kits a year (2× 340020, 1× 340030, 2× 340040), one supplier wanted
Renewal history: asks 1.1-5.4 %, settled 0 % twice, 2.4 %/2.6 % for 2026
Price changes need 90 days' written notice before calendar year end; contract to 2027-06-30 with 12-month auto-extension
Scorecard improving: ppm 371 to 291, OTD 91.8 % vs 95 % target, EUR 150 chargeback per complaint
Gasket 340030 quoted at EUR 1.97/pc, 8 days lead time, not awarded; part qualified with 0 % quota
O-ring set 340020 is 100 % single source; lip seal 340040 is split 50 % with one other source

indicators.credit_index: 167 (12 months ago 167; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 83.7, ppm 371) → 2026Q1 green (otd 86.3, ppm 325) → 2026Q2 green (otd 83.0, ppm 314) → 2026Q3 green (otd 91.8, ppm 291)
